changes: Added a Reset Conversation button that allows starting a fresh chat session while keeping current settings and uploaded datasets intact.
Added a smart floating action button (FAB) that dynamically appears when scrolling long conversations, allowing you to instantly scroll up to the database schema or down to the most recent messages.

Added the MIMIC-III clinical demo as a bundled dataset: a 26-table critical-care database (patients, admissions, ICU stays, lab and chart events, prescriptions, and more) you can pick from the sidebar dataset selector.

This is the project's canonical schema-graph example: questions like "labs for a patient" can join through the patient directly or through a hospital admission, which triggers a join-path clarifying question.
The demo is the openly licensed (ODbL) 100-patient subset; the first load takes a few seconds while the 26 tables are imported and their relationships discovered.

Added a second ambiguity mechanism: when a vague word in your question maps to more than one column of the same kind (for example several dates, prices, or names), the system asks which column you mean before generating SQL.
The new semantic-column check runs after the join-path check and also works on single-CSV datasets, which previously had no pre-SQL ambiguity detection.
Each clarifying question is now tagged with the mechanism that produced it (join-path or semantic-column), and the semantic-column check can be turned off for evaluation.
Added the schema-graph join-path ambiguity mechanism: discovered foreign keys are assembled into a graph and the distinct join paths between the tables a question mentions are enumerated.

Before generating SQL, the system now uses the model to extract the entities in a question, maps them to tables, and asks one clarifying question when more than one join path connects them (for example direct versus through an intermediate table).
Added a sidebar Schema graph panel that lists each table and the tables it joins to, so multi-hop relationships are visible.
The join-path gate runs only on the first round of a multi-table question and degrades to the existing candidate-comparison flow if detection fails.
Added support for local Streamlit secrets in .streamlit/secrets.toml, using OPENROUTER_API_KEY as the hidden default before falling back to the environment.
Restricted the shared default API key to google/gemma-4-31b-it while keeping all model choices available when users enter their own key.
Added an assistant welcome message that introduces the chat when the workspace is empty.
Added a horizontally scrollable database-table browser above the chat, with clickable table names and a three-row read-only preview whose headers expose the column names.
Kept table previews user-controlled by removing the automatic random-table query from startup.
Added a link to the ohadlivay/DB-Whisperer GitHub repository at the top of the sidebar.
Added multi-CSV ingestion: upload several related CSV files (or pick the bundled BikeStores dataset) and query across them in one DuckDB database.

Added automatic foreign-key discovery using naming hints confirmed by value overlap, including self-referential and ambiguous relationships, surfaced to the SQL generator as a RELATIONSHIPS prompt section.
Added a sidebar dataset picker (BikeStores relational, single-CSV student impact, or your own upload) and a relationships panel showing discovered joins with overlap and ambiguity.
Made ingestion robust to messy CSVs: heterogeneous columns reload as text, malformed rows are skipped with an incomplete-discovery warning, and literal NULL text is treated as null.
Added preset, free, and custom OpenRouter model selection with Gemma as the default and relative cost and response-time ratings.
Added a session usage counter that shows the OpenRouter spend delta since the API key was entered and refreshes after model calls.
Improved the chat experience with immediate user messages, persistent scrollable history, and distinct minimal styling for user and assistant responses.
Added the public Streamlit deployment, refreshed GitHub documentation, and introduced a visible version button with a JSON-backed changelog dialog.
Bundled the student-impact dataset as an automatically loaded example that is replaced by an uploaded CSV and restored when the upload is cleared.

Improved ambiguity prompts by deduplicating exact alternatives, using numbered SQL/table sections, limiting table previews to five rows, and forcing clarification questions to choose between represented interpretations.
Passed previous clarification question-and-answer pairs into the ambiguity prompt so repeated questions are avoided.
Skipped the ambiguity LLM call when deduplication leaves fewer than two unique SQL/table alternatives.
Added configurable SQL candidate generation with a default of three candidates and parallel execution to reduce wait time.
Connected the ambiguity layer to the GUI with two clickable clarification options and clarification answers appended to later querier prompts.
Added detailed prompt, response, generation-failure, and execution-failure logging to logs/prompts.jsonl for debugging model and SQL issues.
Improved query failure messages so invalid SQL, failed execution, and invalid model output are easier to diagnose.
Implemented single-CSV ingestion into DuckDB and exposed schema metadata for downstream components.
Implemented schema-aware natural-language-to-SQL generation through OpenRouter using static instructions, schema, top rows, shape, and column statistics.
Added safe read-only SQL validation, query execution, and result display through the application workflow.
Built the first ambiguity service contract for judging executed SQL/result alternatives and returning pass or one two-option clarification question.
Created the high-level architecture document for ETL, ambiguity specification, querying, and GUI integration.
Created the project folder structure and component documentation for the ETLer, Querier, Ambiguity, and GUI modules.
Added a minimal Streamlit interface with a clean query workspace, data and connection status indicators, and placeholders for future workflow features.
Kept the project domain-neutral so it can work with generic CSV data instead of one specific dataset.
